feature: Add a password reset flow to a web app

then.title: Searching forums and docs
then.body: Which library? How does its API work? Why does the example not compile? One search result at a time.

then.title: Writing boilerplate
then.body: Routes, forms, validation and an email template. Necessary, repetitive and slow to type.

then.title: Writing tests
then.body: Happy path, expired links, unknown emails. The first thing to slip when a deadline is close.

then.title: Debugging
then.body: Read the stack trace, add logging, run it again, repeat.

then.title: Review and rework
then.body: A colleague reads the change, asks good questions, and you fix what they find.

thenNote: Roughly two working days for one ordinary feature.

research.title: faster on a set task
research.body: In GitHub’s 2022 controlled experiment, developers with Copilot wrote an HTTP server in JavaScript 56% faster than developers without it.

research.title: more tasks finished at work
research.body: Field trials with 4,867 developers at Microsoft, Accenture and a Fortune 100 company found about 26% more completed tasks with Copilot.

research.title: less time on a complex task
research.body: In Google’s internal trial with 96 engineers, AI features cut the time spent on a complex enterprise task by about 21%.

catch.title: slower, while feeling faster
catch.body: Experienced open-source developers using early-2025 AI assistants took 19% longer on real issues in their own projects, yet believed afterwards that they had been 20% faster.
catch.source: METR, July 2025 (a 2026 follow-up with newer assistants points to a speed-up, but METR calls that data unreliable)

catch.title: delivery stability
catch.body: In the 2024 DORA survey, every 25% more AI adoption went with 7.2% lower delivery stability and 1.5% lower delivery throughput.

catch.title: don’t trust the output
catch.body: 84% of developers use or plan to use AI assistants, but more of them distrust the accuracy of what it produces (46%) than trust it (33%).

factors.title: Focused context
factors.body: Give it the two files that matter, not the whole project or a pasted log.

factors.title: Clear prompts
factors.body: Say where, what is wrong, the limits and what done looks like.

factors.title: The right mode
factors.body: Ask to understand, Plan to design, Agent to change.

factors.title: Reviewing the output
factors.body: Read every change and see the tests pass before you keep it.

factors.title: Keeping the cost down
factors.body: A fresh chat per task and an everyday model for everyday work.

handover: The rest of this session is how to be on the right side of that line.
